name: Jipeng Li
description: Jipeng Li — research on learned representations, generative models, and reliable decisions; photographs of landscapes, wildlife, and life on the road.
research_intro: I study what learned representations tell us about model behavior, and whether they preserve the information needed for reliable decisions.
bio: I am a Ph.D. student in Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of California, Irvine, advised by Yanning Shen. My research interests include graph learning, generative models, and reliable decision-making.
My recent work studies when graph diffusion models can infer noise levels without explicit conditioning, and how graph invariants can support ownership verification for graph neural networks.

Before joining UCI, I completed an M.S. at UC Davis after transitioning from its Ph.D. program, working with Lifeng Lai. I previously earned my master’s degree at Tsinghua University and my bachelor’s degree at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC).
Outside research, I photograph landscapes, wildlife, and the places I pass through.
